title: Credential split across lines by a quoted-printable soft line break in a MIME text part
summary: A SendGrid-shaped key is assigned on one line of a MIME text part whose Content-Transfer-Encoding is quoted-printable. The encoded line is cut at 76 characters by a soft line break (an equal sign ending the line), so the key is written as two fragments with an equal sign and a CRLF between them, and the assignment's own equal sign is written =3D. The key is intact only after quoted-printable decoding.
rationale: The failure mode is a reader that sees the raw lines: it covers only the first fragment (partial-span leakage) or treats the soft-break bytes as part of the value. RFC 2045 section 6.7 rule 5 states that an equal sign as the last character of an encoded line is a non-significant soft line break, so after decoding the key is whole. That holds only for a body whose Content-Transfer-Encoding header names quoted-printable (sections 6.1 and 6.2: the header selects the decoding, and 7bit is assumed when it is absent); the identical bytes in a 7bit part are a value interrupted by a separator that nothing removes, which is the situation of whitespace-inserted-into-credential-value. This is why the Case is kept apart from value-rebuilt-by-the-surrounding-language: the rebuilding is done by a transfer-encoding decode that a header gates, not by a language the carrier is written in, and a separator-split twin differs from it by the header alone. Decode preconditions for any reading that uses the rebuilt value: the part is identified as quoted-printable from its header, a quoted-printable decode is actually run (nothing here says a reader does), and a finding on decoded text is mapped back to the source bytes of both fragments. Out of scope and unresolved: the =XX escapes that can occur inside a value (rule 1; an equal sign in a value is =3D), which the decode vocabulary of the fixture schema cannot represent, and encoded-words in header fields (RFC 2047), which this Case does not cover.

expectation.rationale: RFC 2045 states how quoted-printable text maps back to the original octets; it states nothing about confidentiality or what a reader should cover, so the standard supports the mechanism and no outcome. The candidate reading, recorded on the fixtures as non-asserting data, is must-flag with every fragment covered and the separator bytes (the equal sign and the CRLF) outside the secret: that is the policy that the maintainer decisions for encoded values and for separator-split values already record for other carriers, and whether it extends to a MIME quoted-printable part has not been decided. What would settle it: a maintainer decision (recorded as maintainer-only during the solo-maintainer period) that names this carrier, and a mapping contract with the evaluation consumer that states how a finding on decoded text is mapped to source bytes.

sources.supports: An equal sign as the last character on an encoded line indicates a non-significant (soft) line break in the encoded text; encoded lines are no more than 76 characters long.
sources.locator: 6.7 Quoted-Printable Content-Transfer-Encoding, rule (5) Soft Line Breaks

sources.supports: The Content-Transfer-Encoding value specifies the decoding operation that restores the body to its original form; 7bit is assumed when the field is absent, and 7bit, 8bit and binary mean no encoding transformation was performed.
The US-ASCII equal sign (decimal 61) is represented in quoted-printable as =3D.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Authored from RFC 2045 read on 2026-10-04, before any scanner was consulted. The expectation is unresolved: the standard gives the mechanism, not a confidentiality outcome.
